chunks: That is on account of what you had done in the past; yet God is not unjust to His creatures.

key_terms.بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ يَدَاكَ: what your hands have sent forth (your deeds)

ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'what your hands have sent forth' mean in the context of divine justice?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Al-Hajj underscores the principle of 'Adl (Divine Justice), affirming that retribution is strictly proportional to one's own deeds, not arbitrary divine caprice. It highlights that God’s punishment is a direct consequence of human agency ('what your hands have sent forth'), reinforcing the belief that He is not a Zallam (oppressor) who inflicts unjust suffering upon His servants.
